10.1002_adma.74135: Aqueous batteries are promising for large‐scale energy storage due to inherent safety and low cost; however, their long‐term cycling stability is fundamentally limited by interfacial degradation. Although existing strategies such as “water‐in‐salt” and water–organic hybrid electrolytes can widen the electrochemical stability window (ESW), trace water electrolysis still occurs at the interface, leading to gradual pH drift, electrode dissolution, and eventual battery failure. Here, we propose a self‐regulating interfacial‐boosted electrolyte that effectively addresses these challenges. By introducing phosphate‑based components into wide‑ESW electrolytes, this design autonomously ensures pH stability via intrinsic buffering capability, spontaneously forms a protective cathode–electrolyte interphase in response to metal‐ion dissolution, and reconfigures the ion solvation structure to widen the electrochemical stability window and lowers the interfacial impedance. Demonstrated in a Na 1 . 85 Mn[Fe(CN) 6 ] 0 . 97 ·2H 2 O//NaTi 2 (PO 4 ) 3 full cell with an energy density of 81.7 Wh kg −1 , this electrolyte enables fast charging (75% capacity retention from 1 C to 80 C) and ultra‐long cycling stability (71% capacity retention after 20 000 cycles at 80 C). The strategy offers an effective and generalizable pathway toward high‐performance aqueous batteries.
10.1002_advs.78284: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) for deep‐seated tumors is fundamentally constrained by limited tissue penetration, the ultrashort lifetime of singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ), and the lack of reusable oxygen delivery systems. Herein, we report a near‐infrared (NIR) triggered rechargeable “singlet oxygen battery” that enables sustained and cyclic 1 O 2 supply for enhanced phototherapy. A series of aza‐boron‐dipyrromethene (aza‐BODIPY) probes (NBDP, ABDP, and PBDP) are rationally engineered by integrating distinct 1 O 2 carriers, among which PBDP exhibits optimal performance. Upon 808 nm irradiation (5 min), PBDP nanoparticles (NPs), as the singlet oxygen battery, generate abundant 1 O 2 that is reversibly captured via [4+2] cycloaddition with 2‐pyridone to form endoperoxides (EPOs), while simultaneously enabling efficient photothermal conversion. After light cessation, stored 1 O 2 is thermally released from EPOs for up to 1 h, realizing sustained therapeutic action. Notably, the system supports multiple charging–discharging cycles with negligible performance decay. In vivo NIR‐II imaging reveals efficient tumor accumulation, leading to significant tumor suppression via synergistic sustained PDT/PTT (photothermal therapy) with excellent biocompatibility. This work provides a rechargeable 1 O 2 storage and release platform by integrating NIR activation, self‐heating‐assisted discharge, and cyclic phototherapeutic capability, offering a promising strategy to improve the efficiency and durability of phototherapy for tumor treatment.
10.1002_anie.1697726: Selective photoelectrochemical oxidation of glycerol to dihydroxyacetone (DHA) requires photogenerated holes to reach the substrate faster than they drive oxygen evolution, followed by C–H cleavage without C–C fragmentation. Here, oxygen‐coordinated Ni single atoms on the TiO 2 (001) nanosheet arrays regulate both steps. Isopropanol‐probe and in situ glycerol spectra support Ni‐promoted dissociative adsorption through the secondary hydroxyl group. Radical spectroscopy and interfacial kinetics support subsequent oxidation through glycerol‐derived alkoxy species, accompanied by a 15–20‐fold acceleration of glycerol‐coupled hole transfer and suppressed oxygen evolution. Product‐based glycerol isotope effects supported the kinetic involvement of central C–H cleavage in DHA formation, while calculations showed that Ni coordination increased the energetic preference for C–H over C–C cleavage from 0.05 to 0.38 eV. Operando spectroscopy and weaker DHA adsorption support retention of the three‐carbon skeleton and product release. Under charge‐normalized conditions, the Ni single‐atom photoanode achieved a DHA Faradaic efficiency of approximately 66.6%, compared with 22.2% for unmodified TiO 2 and 16.4% for the NiO x control. DHA‐selective charge utilization persisted in recirculating‐flow operation with 0.5 M glycerol. These results support coupled control over substrate adsorption and subsequent bond selectivity as a design principle for selective PEC polyol oxidation.
10.1002_anie.9133941: Photoelectrocatalytic (PEC) organic synthesis has emerged as a promising platform for sustainable chemical manufacturing by synergistically integrating light and electrical energy. The fundamental mechanism involves the generation of electron-hole pairs in semiconductor photoelectrodes, where photogenerated holes drive oxidative transformations at the anode and electrons facilitate reductive reactions at the cathode. This approach enables precise control over reaction pathways under mild conditions, offering enhanced energy efficiency, improved selectivity and elimination of stoichiometric oxidants. This review comprehensively summarizes the rapid development of PEC organic synthesis, beginning with its fundamental principles and common photoelectrode fabrication techniques. Recent advances are then outlined across two major domains: the photoanode-mediated oxidation of single molecules (e.g., alcohols, biomass-derived platform chemicals, alkenes, and C─H bonds) and photoelectrochemical cross-coupling reactions for constructing C─X (X = C, N, P, Cl, and Br) bonds. Finally, a forward-looking perspective on critical challenges and future directions are discussed, which will significantly improve the insight for future development of PEC organic synthesis.
10.1002_smll.202509270: Persistent interfacial instability remains a critical bottleneck for solid‐state lithium metal batteries, necessitating electrolyte designs that simultaneously regulate bulk transport and interfacial reactions. A fluorination‐decoupling strategy is proposed by integrating fluorinated metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) with Lewis‐acidic sites into PVDF‐HFP quasi‐solid‐state electrolytes to tailor Li + solvation dynamics and induce robust interfacial protection. Experimental results confirmed that the electron‑withdrawing and sterically bulky fluorinated moieties disrupted the metal–oxygen coordination environment and enhanced the Lewis acidity of the MOF. These modifications limited anion mobility, promoted ion‑pair dissociation, and weakened Li + coordination. Moreover, preferential interactions with fluorosilane facilitated the formation of a solid electrolyte interphase rich in LiF without compromising bulk conductivity (1.16 × 10 −3 S cm −1 at 30 °C). These mechanistic insights translated into outstanding cycling stability: Li||Li symmetric cells operated stably for over 2200 h at 0.2 mA cm −2 , while Li||LiFePO 4 and Li||NCM811 retained 93.5% and 70.0% capacity after 2000 and 450 cycles at 20C and 5C, respectively. This study provides a new avenue to tailor Li + solvation and improves interfacial stability in solid‐state electrolytes by precise control of fluorine–framework interactions.
10.1016_j.esci.2026.100643: The CO 2 electroreduction reaction (CO 2 RR) is one of the sustainable technology paths to achieve CO 2 utilization and carbon-negative reduction. However, there is still a large gap between the fundamental research on the CO 2 RR system and its practical applications. From the perspective of chemical process intensification, the CO 2 RR system needs to adopt a new technical way to eliminate that gap. In this review, we highlight recent advances in process intensification strategies for upgrading the CO 2 RR system to the industrial level, based on the rational construction of catalyst designs and coupled processes. We categorize this progress according to three aspects: feedstock process optimization, reaction process intensification, and product engineering. The review closes by summing up the remaining challenges and discussing the upcoming prospects for the CO 2 RR system. This paper thus outlines process intensification strategies ranging from catalyst design to process coupling to reshape the CO 2 RR system and guide its design and optimization in the future.
10.1016_j.est.2026.123879: The simultaneous realization of mechanical flexibility, optical transparency, and electrochemical stability remains a critical challenge for next-generation wearable electronics. Herein, we demonstrate a mechanically robust transparent supercapacitor with electrochromic capability based on an optimized WO₃/ITO/PET heterostructure coupled with a LiCl-doped PVDF-co-HFP membrane electrolyte. By precisely tuning the active WO₃ layer thickness to 300 nm on ITO/PET substrates, the electrode architecture effectively buffers mechanical strain while ensuring homogeneous ion transport, yielding a high areal capacitance of 42 mF cm −2 at 0.1 mA cm −2 . When assembled into a symmetric device, the solid-state system operates within a wide potential window of ±2.5 V and exhibits extraordinary mechanical endurance, retaining 94% of its initial capacitance after 20,000 bending cycles ( r = 3 mm), significantly outperforming conventional gel-based counterparts. These results establish the optimized WO₃/ITO/PET architecture as a promising, highly durable platform for transparent and deformable energy storage systems.
10.1021_jacs.5c14127: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER), the anodic half-reaction in water electrolysis, remains a critical bottleneck to the widespread adoption of a hydrogen-based economy. While spin polarization of reaction intermediates has been shown to enhance the performance of the OER, existing studies often overlook the distinctions between different ways of spin-polarizing intermediates and their correlation with catalytic efficiency. In this study, we conduct a comprehensive analysis of spin-mediated catalysis, revealing that the efficiency of the OER is highly sensitive to the nature and magnitude of the spin polarization applied. More significantly, we explore the interplay among different methods for generating spin polarization at catalysts and demonstrate how their combination can have a constructive or destructive impact on catalytic performance. To provide deeper insight into the mechanisms driving spin-controlled catalysis, we interpreted these findings using a statistical model.
10.1039_d6ta03588d: MoSe 2 @NC nanocomposites were fabricated via a solvothermal process followed by in situ carbon coating and annealing, delivering outstanding electrochemical performance as anode materials for sodium-ion batteries.
10.1039_d6ta05162f: A one-pot hydrothermal strategy realizes dual regulation of layered ammonium vanadate. Sulfur heteroatoms tune intralattice electronic interface; glycine intercalation rebuilds interlayer interface for synchronous modulation and skeleton reinforcement.
